Q: git 'unmerged paths' - resolve strategy needed A:

It seems you have one unsolved merge that you need to handle by yourself. The full message you posted in the link (and the highlighted part you posted in your question) says you need to manually resolve the conflict on file prepare_step_server.yml.

I advise you to look for an editor that has support for git diff - I like Intellij Idea or Visual Studio Code, both free (comunity) versions. It is helpful, but if you don't want them, you just need to open in any editor and fix the conflicting lines (you need to search the file for it, you will see some text markers showing the conflicting line you need to fix) and make a new commit. Maybe this tutorial or this other question can help you, if you are still lost...

EDIT:

Since you mentioned you like VIM, maybe this post might help you. It is about vimdiff, and how to use it as a merge tool. As a start you would need to make it your default merge tool doing the following:

git config merge.tool vimdiff
git config merge.conflictstyle diff3
git config mergetool.prompt false

Then you can just use the command git mergetool to open the editor's UI. It uses this terminology in the UI, in case you get lost with it:

LOCAL – this is file from the current branch

BASE – common ancestor, how file looked before both changes

REMOTE – file you are merging into your branch

MERGED – merge result, this is what gets saved in the repo

The post previously mentioned have more details on that - the user that made the question seemed kind of lost when trying to merge with it, and the accepted answer explains in details.

Q: MySql mysql.h file not found in VS2008 C++ A:

1 - make sure you actually have MySQL's header files installed. Typically, these are located in the 'include' directory of your mysql installation.

2 - Set your Visual Studio C++ project settings to include that include directory for use by C++ projects.

Add your mysql include directories to the box.

Tool->Options->Projects and Settings->VC++ Directories. Then on the right hand side, Open the dropbox labeled "Show Directories For" and pick "Include Files". Here's a screen shot of that window.

Additionally, you will probably want to set up Library directories to include MySQL's `'lib' folder as well, so that later on your builds can find the mysql libraries to link against.

Q: How to implement rollback of multi-statement transaction in SQLite? A:

I find this question reasonable and 'm a bit surprised it has taken so little attention. I recently started learning SQLite. And this is what I can contribute with.

First of all, let's see what the documentation says:

Transactions can be started manually using the BEGIN command. Such transactions usually persist until the next COMMIT or ROLLBACK command. But a transaction will also ROLLBACK if the database is closed or if an error occurs and the ROLLBACK conflict resolution algorithm is specified.

So you understand this part correctly. However, in the corresponding section describing the ON CONFLICT clause one can read:

The ON CONFLICT clause is allowed on UNIQUE, NOT NULL, and PRIMARY KEY constraints only. The ON CONFLICT clause is not allowed on CHECK and FOREIGN KEY constraints.

So it seems that you cannot use it on CHECK constraint.

Tests

Let's create a table:

create table if not exists jobs (
  name     text           not null,
  billable real           not null,
  count    integer unique not null);

So name and billable must not be null, and count additionally must be unique.

Let's insert violating either constraint:

begin;
insert into jobs values("foo", 1.5, 1);
insert into jobs values(null, 1.5, 2);
Runtime error: NOT NULL constraint failed: jobs.name (19)
commit;
select * from jobs;
foo|1.5|1

So we see that the first insert has been committed. Let's do the same from scratch but specifying rollback algorithm:

create table if not exists jobs (
  name     text           not null on conflict rollback,
  billable real           not null on conflict rollback,
  count    integer unique not null on conflict rollback);

Now let's insert:

begin;
insert into jobs values("foo", 1.5, 1);
insert into jobs values(null, 1.5, 2);
Runtime error: NOT NULL constraint failed: jobs.name (19)
commit;
Runtime error: cannot commit - no transaction is active
select * from jobs;

See how the commit statement produces an error already -- the transaction had been rolled back by the time you tried to commit it. You can also try for the UNIQUE constraint.

Solution

As pointed out by @mdisibio when you use some API/Binding you can look at the result of executing any statement and if failed then rollback the transaction. I would suggest using some kind of wrapper/RAII/decorator (depending on what the language provides). I will show a pseudo code snippet:

function transaction (f)
  return function (...)
    connection.exec('BEGIN')
    result = f(...)
    if result != OK then
      connection.exec('ROLLBACK')
      return

    connection.exec('COMMIT')

and then wrap your function:

insertAllOrNothing = transaction (
function (items)
  for item in items
    if connection.exec('INSERT INTO jobs VALUES(item)') != OK then
      return FAIL
  return OK
)

then call

insertAllOrNothing([foo, bar, baz])

Tested with sqlite version 3.45.1

Q: Can firebird database connect to other databases using like linked server in SQL Server? A:

Firebird doesn't have a linked server feature. There is a limited method for accessing other Firebird databases (either remote or locally) using EXECUTE STATEMENT, however this only supports Firebird databases, and you need to provide the data source information on each invocation.

Q: Flutter Icons 3 dots A:

You will find it on https://api.flutter.dev/flutter/material/Icons-class.html. In short, use these vertical three-dot icons, which are used today as:

        Icon(Icons.more_vert),
        Icon(Icons.more_vert_outlined),
        Icon(Icons.more_vert_rounded),
        Icon(Icons.more_vert_sharp),
